why: Both wrapped the single AsyncOpenAI chokepoint and verified all five call sites live, but A's system-level judgment is better grounded: it measured that the runtime already sets prompt_cache_key on Anthropic models (so B's headline 'biggest lever' cache policy is largely a no-op, and B's gpt-4o-mini probe had no no-key control — A measured -49% with or without), it refused blind cross-vendor fallbacks because the model here is operator config, and its built items fix real app-specific bugs (screenshots silently dropped for any post-2024 model, plus the data:image/jpeg mislabel that 400s on Anthropic). B ships more default coverage and a genuine retry-predicate bug fix with tests, but derives unlock_hosts from the configured base_url including localhost, which sends a self-hosted/Ollama deployment's prompts to a third party whenever its model name matches a catalog id (gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-v4-flash) — exactly the case A scoped out by name, and B asserts it is safe on a false premise.
A_best: Depth of measured negative results — prompt_cache_key, Flex, provider_timeout and fallbacks each rejected with a reason specific to this app (runtime already sets the cache key; the model is a deployment setting, not a constant), and the vision item found and fixed a second latent bug (PNG labelled as JPEG) with before/after live evidence, including a kept failing intermediate run.
B_best: The retry-predicate finding: retry_if_exception_type((OpenAIError, Exception, ValueError)) matches everything, so a token-limit error that cannot clear itself was retried six times with ~3 minutes of backoff — correctly diagnosed, fixed at all three entry points plus the agent's handler, and covered by two new tests; i7 (Router count_tokens instead of cl100k guesses for the max_input_tokens guard) is also a sharp, app-specific lever A never considered.
A_worst: The shipped migration only treats api.openai.com as routable, so deployments following this repo's own README (Anthropic-compatible endpoint, Jiekou, PPIO, Google) move nothing until an unapplied branch lands — real coverage is narrower than the headline, and A added no tests for any of it.
B_worst: unlock_hosts from base_url unlocks localhost (its own test asserts it), and the claim that catalog-only routing keeps self-hosted deployments untouched is wrong for locally served catalog-named models — a prompt-egress change shipped in the migration itself; compounding this, the fixed fallback list [claude-sonnet-4-6, gpt-4.1-mini] is applied to every deployment's unknown primary model and even to ask_with_images, with no check that the candidates accept the request's images.
